name: Counter Rotating Discs as Sources of Vacuum Fields
description: Two regions of a known vacuum field joined across a thin disc. A displaced cut and reflection can produce positive surface density and two streams of ordinary matter circling in opposite senses.
convention: We use $G=c=1$ and the Ricci contraction $R_{\mu\nu}=R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$. A dot denotes differentiation along an affine parameter.
history: Werner Israel constructed an equatorial disc source for the Kerr-Newman field in 1970 [israel1970]. The disc spans the ring singularity [israel1970]. A displaced cut and reflection join two regions of a known vacuum field across a thin disc. The cut lies clear of the singularity, and the disc's matter supplies the jump in normal derivatives [ledvinka2019discs].¶Jiří Bičák, Donald Lynden-Bell, and Joseph Katz applied this construction to static fields in 1993, showing that "most vacuum Weyl solutions can arise as the metrics of counter-rotating relativistic disks" [bicak1993]. Their examples include the Curzon, Schwarzschild, and Zipoy-Voorhees fields [bicak1993]. Bičák, Lynden-Bell, and Christophe Pichon also constructed relativistic discs from potentials used for flat galaxy models that year [bicak1993b].¶Two streams with equal densities and equal opposite speeds can support a static disc without radial pressure. Their angular momenta cancel, and their orbital motion supplies azimuthal pressure without radial pressure [ledvinka2019discs]. The same Schwarzschild vacuum geometry can therefore surround a spherical body or form the two sides of a disc junction [bicak1993]. The global geometry includes the disc and the identification across it.¶In units $G = c = 1$, the Weyl potentials are $U$ and $k$, with derivatives evaluated just above the disc at $z = 0$. The surface energy density is $\varepsilon = e^{U-k}U_{,z}(1-\rho U_{,\rho})/(2\pi)$, and the azimuthal pressure is $p_\phi = e^{U-k}U_{,z}\rho U_{,\rho}/(2\pi)$ [ledvinka2019discs]. Here $\rho$ is the cylindrical radius, and each stream has speed $v^2 = p_\phi/\varepsilon$ measured by a static observer. Positive densities and speeds below light require $\varepsilon > p_\phi \ge 0$, which also satisfies the dominant and weak energy conditions. Each stream's proper rest surface density is $(\varepsilon-p_\phi)/2$ [bicak1993kerr, ledvinka2019discs].¶Bičák and Tomáš Ledvinka extended the construction to rotation in 1993 and showed that these discs "can act as exact sources of all types of the Kerr metric" [bicak1993kerr]. Their discs extend to infinity with finite mass, and frame dragging makes the two streams asymmetric. In the local frame where the surface stress is diagonal, equal opposite speeds reproduce the azimuthal pressure [bicak1993kerr]. For the displaced cuts, the singular region lies in the discarded slab, and suitable choices of the cut admit positive density and matter moving below light speed [bicak1993kerr, ledvinka2019discs].¶José P. S. Lemos and Patricio S. Letelier superposed thin discs and black holes in 1994 [lemosletelier1994]. Their annular discs have an inner edge and admit configurations with matter moving below light speed; equal counterrotating populations have zero net angular momentum [lemosletelier1994]. A negligible disc mass leaves the geometry of a black hole with a disc of test particles [lemosletelier1994].¶Pichon and Lynden-Bell allowed radial pressure by joining curved surfaces in 1996 [pichonlyndenbell1996]. They constructed rotating discs with pressure support, including sources of the Kerr geometry [pichonlyndenbell1996]. Ledvinka, Martin Žofka, and Bičák extended the identification method to Kerr-Newman fields in a 1998 preprint published in 1999 [ledvinkazofkabicak1999]. Charged rings with internal pressure or two streams on circular electrogeodesics can supply both the gravitational field and the electromagnetic field [ledvinkazofkabicak1999].¶Letelier extended cut and reflection to magnetostatic fields in 1999 [letelier1999magnetic]. The disc carries azimuthal pressure and electric current, with no radial pressure [letelier1999magnetic]. Guillermo A. González and Letelier generated finite static discs with radial pressure or radial tension through conformal maps in a 1998 preprint published in 1999 [gonzalezletelier1999stress]. Their radial pressure examples have negative surface density near the rim [gonzalezletelier1999stress].¶Finite discs with two rigidly counterrotating dust streams also admit exact exterior fields expressed through hyperelliptic theta functions [kleinrichter1999]. The relative densities of the streams vary continuously across this family [kleinrichter1999]. González and Letelier constructed rotating thin discs from the Kerr and Taub-NUT geometries in 2000 [gonzalezletelier2000]. Christian Klein expressed the junction conditions for finite counterrotating dust discs as boundary data for the stationary vacuum field in 2001 [klein2001]. Jörg Frauendiener and Klein calculated masses, angular momenta, and stream velocities for the finite disc family in 2001 [frauendienerklein2001].¶Klein generated charged members of the finite disc family through a Harrison transformation in 2002 [klein2002charged]. Positive stream densities and timelike electrogeodesics restrict the charge and rotation parameters [klein2002charged]. Klein expressed stationary black hole and annular disc geometries through hyperelliptic theta functions in 2003 [klein2003blackhole]. Their discs extend to infinity, and the black hole lies inside a finite inner edge [klein2003blackhole].¶González and Omar A. Espitia analysed static discs with radial pressure as two counterrotating perfect fluids in 2003 [gonzalezespitia2003]. The stresses constrain the product of the stream velocities; a further physical condition is needed to determine both velocities [gonzalezespitia2003]. Equal opposite speeds and circular geodesic motion require additional restrictions on these pressure supported fluids [gonzalezespitia2003].¶Gonzalo García-Reyes and González extended the charged dust interpretation to static electrovacuum discs in 2004 [garciareyes2004static]. Purely electric or purely magnetic examples admit equal opposite electrogeodesic speeds; combined fields can require unequal speeds [garciareyes2004static]. García-Reyes and González also represented charged discs with radial pressure as two counterrotating perfect fluids that year [garciareyes2004fluid]. Their finite examples have positive energy density near the centre and negative energy density near the rim [garciareyes2004fluid].¶Maximiliano Ujevic and Letelier perturbed the matter in Chazy-Curzon and Zipoy-Voorhees discs in 2004 and found unstable modes with the background metric held fixed [ujevicletelier2004]. Their fluid perturbations include the collective response of the matter [ujevicletelier2004]. A Schwarzschild black hole, a Chazy-Curzon disc, and two axial rods representing jets form an exact static superposition studied in 2005 [vogtletelier2005]. The rods change the radial stability of circular orbits in the disc [vogtletelier2005].¶García-Reyes and González decomposed stationary electrovacuum disc stresses and currents into two charged streams in 2007 [garciareyesgonzalez2007]. Their Kerr-Newman examples have a diagonalizable surface stress with purely azimuthal pressure [garciareyesgonzalez2007]. Circular electrogeodesics satisfy the stress constraint when the charged streams can follow timelike circular orbits [garciareyesgonzalez2007].¶González and Antonio Calixto Gutiérrez-Piñeres superposed an annular dust disc and a Schwarzschild black hole in 2008 [gonzalezgutierrez2008]. Its counterrotating streams remain timelike when the inner edge lies outside the circular photon orbit [gonzalezgutierrez2008]. González and coauthors generated an infinite family of annular dust potentials in oblate spheroidal coordinates in 2009 [gonzalez2009annular]. García-Reyes and González included charged and magnetized Kerr-NUT sources with tangential heat flow in 2009 [garciareyes2009kerrnut].¶Oldřich Semerák and Petra Suková followed timelike geodesics around black holes surrounded by counterrotating annular discs in 2010 [semeraksukova2010chaos]. They found regular islands and chaotic layers whose extent depends on the disc mass, inner radius, and particle energy [semeraksukova2010chaos]. The dependence is nonmonotonic; a larger disc mass can restore regular motion in parts of the phase space [semeraksukova2010chaos].¶Reinaldo J. Gleiser identified a curvature singularity and an infinite source of negative mass at the inner edge of the 2009 annular dust family in 2012 [gleiser2012comment]. The isolated dust discs have vanishing ADM mass [gleiser2012comment]. González and Gutiérrez-Piñeres extended the interpretation as two counterrotating perfect fluids to rotating discs with radial pressure in 2012 [gonzalezgutierrez2012pressure]. They obtained the stream velocities for geodesic motion and for equal opposite speeds, and constructed disc sources from the Kerr field [gonzalezgutierrez2012pressure].¶Semerák and Suková compared recurrence diagnostics for black hole and annular disc geodesics in 2012, and Suková and Semerák calculated Lyapunov exponents and orbital divergence indicators in 2013 [semeraksukova2012chaos, sukovasemerak2013chaos]. Their diagnostics distinguish trajectories that linger near regular islands before entering larger chaotic regions [semeraksukova2012chaos, sukovasemerak2013chaos]. Gutiérrez-Piñeres decomposed the surface stress and electric current of a static charged disc into two perfect fluid contributions in a 2013 preprint [gutierrez2013twofluids].¶Gutiérrez-Piñeres and coauthors superposed static black holes and thin discs in a magnetic field in 2014 [gutierrez2014magnetic]. The magnetic field enlarges the regions of superluminal counter rotation and radial instability in their examples [gutierrez2014magnetic]. Cosimo Bambi and coauthors used a light Lemos-Letelier disc to estimate biases in black hole spin measurements in 2014 [bambi2014spin]. With the inner disc edge at the innermost stable circular orbit, the disc mass raises the radiative efficiency and can mimic a small black hole spin [bambi2014spin]. Semerák and coauthors compared the annular disc dynamics with pseudo-Newtonian black hole potentials in 2015 [witzany2015chaos]. The Paczyński-Wiita and logarithmic potentials reproduce several resonance patterns, with different thresholds and accessible regions of phase space [witzany2015chaos].¶Ronaldo S. S. Vieira, Javier Ramos-Caro, and Alberto Saa derived a vertical stability criterion for circular timelike geodesics in static thin disc geometries in 2016 [vieiraramoscarosaa2016]. The strong energy condition on the disc suffices for vertical stability of these orbits [vieiraramoscarosaa2016]. They also obtained an approximate third integral for nearby orbits from the adiabatic invariance of the vertical action [vieiraramoscarosaa2016].¶Eduar A. Becerra and coauthors used the Komar mass to choose the cutoff radius in fluid perturbations of static discs in 2017 [becerra2017mass]. The Chazy-Curzon and Zipoy-Voorhees examples retained unstable modes under this choice [becerra2017mass]. Vanessa P. de Freitas and Saa constructed magnetized discs from the Gutsunaev-Manko geometry that year, reflecting the electromagnetic potential so that surface currents support the magnetic field without magnetic monopoles [freitassaa2017]. Their allowed parameter region admits circular orbits stable against radial and vertical perturbations [freitassaa2017]. Collective perturbations of the magnetized disc matter require an equation of state [freitassaa2017].¶Pavel Čížek and Semerák expressed the first order perturbation of a Schwarzschild black hole by a light rotating annular disc in 2017 [cizeksemerak2017]. They integrated ring Green functions in closed form to obtain the gravitational potential and frame dragging [cizeksemerak2017]. Petr Kotlařík, Semerák, and Čížek calculated the horizon distortion and shifts of circular orbits in this geometry in 2018 [kotlarik2018rotating]. Their counterrotating dust interpretation requires positive stream densities and timelike circular orbits [kotlarik2018rotating].¶Ledvinka and Bičák applied the identification method to the first three Tomimatsu-Sato geometries in 2019 [ledvinka2019discs]. They distinguished equal opposite speeds in the frame that diagonalizes the surface stress, which require radial momentum exchange, from two freely orbiting streams [ledvinka2019discs]. Two circular timelike geodesics with positive stream densities impose additional restrictions on the disc parameters [ledvinka2019discs].¶Suková and coauthors tested a curvature criterion for geodesic chaos in the black hole and annular disc geometry in 2019 [polcar2019chaos]. Chaotic trajectories can cross the disc even when the regions selected as unstable by the criterion lie outside the accessible phase space [polcar2019chaos]. Vieira generated annular discs around a Schwarzschild black hole from seeds containing several collinear Weyl rods in a 2019 preprint published in 2020 [vieira2020seeds]. The central black hole survives the cut and reflection, and the counterrotating streams become superluminal near the horizon [vieira2020seeds].¶Pedro V. P. Cunha and coauthors traced light rays around a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a Lemos-Letelier disc in 2020 [cunha2020lensing]. A heavier disc bends light towards its plane, broadens the image of the thin disc, and makes the black hole shadow more prolate for an equatorial observer [cunha2020lensing]. Light rays crossing a transparent disc can oscillate across the plane before escaping to different regions of the distant sky [cunha2020lensing].¶Kotlařík, David Kofroň, and Semerák constructed static thin discs with power law density profiles in 2022 [kotlarik2022powerlaw]. Their potentials are explicit for both finite discs and annular discs extending to infinity [kotlarik2022powerlaw]. Kotlařík and Kofroň obtained closed expressions for both Weyl potentials of a Schwarzschild black hole with a disc of infinite extent and finite mass in 2022 [kotlarikkofron2022]. They used Kelvin inversions and superpositions of Kuzmin-Toomre discs, whose density falls to zero at the black hole and at infinity [kotlarikkofron2022]. The circular dust interpretation applies only where the counterrotating streams remain timelike [kotlarikkofron2022].¶Che-Yu Chen and Kotlařík calculated massless scalar quasinormal modes of a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a gravitating disc in 2023 [chenkotlarik2023]. To first order in the ratio of disc mass to black hole mass, the disc lowers the oscillation frequency and lengthens the damping time in the configurations they studied [chenkotlarik2023]. Eddy Brandon de León, Frauendiener, and Klein traced light rays through the finite counterrotating dust disc geometries in 2024 [deleon2024]. Their images show gravitational lensing and frame dragging around opaque discs [deleon2024].¶Enrico Cannizzaro, Valerio De Luca, and Paolo Pani calculated the response of black hole disc geometries to external scalar and electromagnetic fields in 2024 [cannizzaro2024tidal]. The disc produces nonzero tidal Love numbers, which relate the induced multipoles to the applied fields [cannizzaro2024tidal]. Avijit Chowdhury and coauthors extended the scalar and electromagnetic calculations to reflecting compact objects surrounded by these discs in a 2026 preprint [chowdhury2026tidal]. A vanishing scalar field at the surface preserves the logarithmic dependence of the response on the fractional surface separation from the Schwarzschild radius [chowdhury2026tidal].¶Yin-Da Guo and coauthors calculated massive scalar quasibound states around black holes surrounded by these discs in a 2026 preprint [guo2026quasibound]. They obtained shifts in the oscillation frequencies and decay rates to first order in the disc mass [guo2026quasibound]. For a disc much larger than the scalar cloud, the spatial metric changes the decay rate as well as the gravitational redshift [guo2026quasibound].¶Kofroň, Kotlařík, and Semerák generated exact static thin disc fields by convolving weighted Appell ring potentials in a 2023 preprint published in 2026 [kofron2023]. They obtained both Weyl potentials explicitly for several discs and their superpositions with a Schwarzschild black hole [kofron2023]. The Newtonian surface density fixes the convolution weight through an Abel transform [kofron2023]. Claudia Caputo and Ledvinka studied bound geodesics around a Schwarzschild black hole perturbed by a rotating thin disc in 2026 [caputoledvinka2026]. The disc edges and frame dragging change the degree of geodesic chaos in their model [caputoledvinka2026].

related.text: Israel's seam spans Kerr's ring and carries negative mass moving faster than light [israel1970]. A displaced cut removes the singular region and permits a disc with positive density and matter moving below light speed [bicak1993kerr].
Two retained regions of Kerr's vacuum geometry meet across the matter disc. The location of the cut determines the surface stress and the admissible streams [bicak1993kerr, ledvinka2019discs].
Schwarzschild's vacuum field supplies both sides of a static disc junction [bicak1993]. The seam's equal opposite streams carry no net angular momentum.
The Curzon field is a Weyl seed for a counter rotating disc [bicak1993]. Displacing the cut excludes the seed's singularity from both retained regions.

The Zipoy-Voorhees Weyl fields also admit disc sources constructed by a displaced cut and reflection [bicak1993]. The cut and the seed parameters determine whether the matter is physically admissible.

parameters.description: Reflected Weyl potential, evaluated from the seed at $(\rho,b+|z|)$; $U_{,\rho\rho}+U_{,\rho}/\rho+U_{,zz}=0$ off the seam
Reflected Weyl potential; $k_{,\rho}=\rho(U_{,\rho}^2-U_{,z}^2)$ and $k_{,z}=2\rho U_{,\rho}U_{,z}$ off the seam
Positive displacement of the cut, a length
Mass parameter of the vacuum seed, a length
Half length of the Weyl rod, a length

coordinates.convention: Coordinates are $(t,\rho,\phi,z)$, with $t$, $\rho$, and $z$ lengths and $\phi$ an angle. The two retained regions meet at $z=0$; the potentials are composed with $b+|z|$. Smooth tensor components apply at $z\ne0$; the surface stress on the seam follows from the jump in extrinsic curvature.
